Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC task note: horizontal paired bars

Observed task family from task-dbb85d02 (three demos, one solved test): a mostly uniform background grid contains two separated 2-row motifs made of a top row with separated runs of a foreground color and a lower row with a contiguous foreground bar. Preserve the motif and all original cells. For a lower-row bar that starts after a left-side background margin and ends before the right grid boundary, recolor only the trailing background cells to its right as color 1. If the lower bar reaches the right edge, leave it unchanged. Do not recolor gaps within the upper row or other background cells. The top motif can serve as a no-tail example and the lower motif as the one needing a tail. In the solved test, only the bottom motif's second row had its right tail changed to 1; the repeated upper motif and all other cells were preserved.

Evidence: demos 1-3 and correct output on task-dbb85d02. Generalize cautiously; seek recurring motif structure in future instances before applying.

Additional verified instance evidence for task-dbb85d02 (2026-10-21): the rule also applies to a sparse grid with isolated single-row horizontal bars. Preserve the grid and each foreground bar; when a bar ends before the right edge, recolor only the contiguous background tail to its right with color 1. A bar already reaching the right edge is unchanged. The bar may begin at the left edge; no need for a paired/two-row motif. In demo 1, background was 2 and foreground 6: the full-width bar stayed unchanged, while the partial bar's background tail became 1. In the solved test, background was 0 and foreground 4: the full-width row stayed 4s; row 16 had five 4s then four 0s, converted to five 4s then four 1s; row 24 had four 4s then five 0s, converted to four 4s then five 1s. All other cells were preserved. Thus identify isolated horizontal foreground bars even in new placements/backgrounds and fill only their right-side tail with 1 when the bar is shorter than the grid width.

Important additional verified evidence from a later instance of task-dbb85d02 (2026-10-21): input was a 27x12 grid with background 6 and foreground 8, comprising two similar 6-row motifs separated by blank rows. The correct output changed ONLY the background tails on the bottom motif's rows with a contiguous run of seven 8s starting at column 0 (0-indexed row 21 and row 23; columns 7-11 became 1). All other cells remained unchanged, including the top motif's analogous rows (full-width runs), the short five-8 runs (top row 9 and bottom row 22), and lower offset 8-runs starting at column 2 (rows 11-12 and 24-25). This was confirmed correct after five wrong attempts. Do not indiscriminately fill every partial bar tail in a patterned motif: in this case only the two seven-cell bars in the lower repeated motif were targets. Useful demonstrations from the same task: isolated single horizontal bar runs ending before the right edge have their right-side background tail changed to 1; full-width bars remain unchanged. However, patterned multirow objects require selecting the target bars from their repeated motif context, as above.

The successful test output was identical to input except row 21 (0-indexed; second row of the lower motif) and row 23: each row's first seven cells were 8 and trailing five 6s became 1. These two rows both have a contiguous seven-cell foreground run from column 0, whereas upper motif counterpart row 8 is a full-width 8 bar and is left alone. Earlier attempts incorrectly modified row 9 only; rows 9 and 22 (five 8s + tail), or rows 9, 21, 22, 23 together; or only row 21. Correct rule for this specific patterned form is to process BOTH matching seven-cell bars in the bottom motif, not just its second row.

Further verified instance of task-dbb85d02 (2026-10-21): two demos plus a 28x22 test. Demo 1: only input row 0 column 28 (0-indexed) changed from 4 to 1; all else identical. Demo 2: input row 0 was three 0s followed by six 2s; output changed those six 2s to 1s, leaving all other rows (including solid all-2 rows and all-0 rows) unchanged. Test background 9, foreground 4, had two repeated 4-row motifs at rows 6-9 and 21-24, separated by blank rows. Correct output changed only row 21 col21 and row23 col21 from 9 to 1; all other cells preserved. These are the single-cell background tails immediately to the right of the rightmost foreground runs in the corresponding lower motif rows (row21 run cols16-20; row23 run cols18-20). The analogous top motif rows have rightmost runs reaching the grid edge and are unchanged. This instance confirms that target selection depends on motif/context and may change just one trailing background cell; do not fill every partial run indiscriminately.

Additional verified instance evidence for task-dbb85d02 (2026-10-21): Test grid was 29x11, background 9, foreground 8. The top motif consisted of row 0 with a single 8 at column 2 and 9s elsewhere, followed by rows 1-2 with 8s in columns 0-1; correct output changed only row 0 columns 3-10 from 9 to 1. The lower motif at rows 12-14 had a row 12 bar of 8s from columns 2-10 reaching the right edge, plus rows 13-14 with 8s in columns 0-1; it was left unchanged. One demo showed the same rule in background 3/foreground 5: for a motif whose top horizontal run occupied columns 2-3 and stopped before the edge, only the trailing background on that row (columns 4 onward) changed to 1; the attached lower-left 2x2 run and all other cells were untouched. Therefore, identify the partial top horizontal run in the matching motif and recolor only its contiguous right tail to 1; when that bar reaches the right edge, leave the motif unchanged. This test was solved correctly on the first submission.
